annotation.evidence_span: MAY drop these packets, or MAY buffer them in anticipation of later packets
annotation.interpretation_a: The client can choose to discard out-of-order packets immediately.
annotation.interpretation_b: The client can choose to buffer out-of-order packets, potentially consuming memory, in hopes of receiving the necessary key material later.
annotation.justification: The MAY/MAY construction allows for two valid implementations: immediate dropping or buffering. The lack of constraints on buffering (duration, resource limits) creates a potential vulnerability.
annotation.missing_information: There is no limit on how long the client should buffer packets, or any guidance on how to manage buffer resources. This could lead to denial-of-service if an attacker sends many out-of-order packets.
